method: one reviewer (second-check fixes; audit of the new figures with own scripts; appendix regenerated) followed by a skeptic

findings.title: The in-range heat overages are put down to 'the trained 3-8 deg ramps' and to x1.1 mass, without the caveat that all three skeptics asked for
findings.evidence: My script review_d22final3/main/scripts/inrange.py reads the limits from each run record's env_config. It reproduces 0/2/4/11, 31/28/35/1 and 0/0 of 37, and the values 1.006-1.064 (mass x1.1) and 1.020 / 1.035-1.155 / 1.096-1.216 (ramps). Every in-range overage for 128 s1 (mass1.1 1.0061, ramp8 1.0201) and s2 (mass1.1 1.0219, ramps 1.0354/1.073/1.1553) is either a ramp or the every-body mass point. The sweep's ramp is one box with half-length L = 10 m, starting 0.6 m ahead (robustness/sweep.py:182-187), so the policy climbs for the whole window. Training up-ramps are 0.8-2.0 m long, followed by a plateau and a down-ramp (trike_env.py@f84a6919:196-198, 374-383). Training draws mass per body (f84a6919:724, size=m.nbody). My Monte Carlo on fore128.xml (21 bodies, 200k draws) gives a total-mass scale SD of 0.0286 and a maximum of 1.076, so training never saw x1.1 on the whole robot. The A1, NEW1 and RD1 verdicts each said not to call the ramps simply inside the training ranges. The text says 'the trained 3-8 deg ramps' and 'Run 3's leg stayed under at every trained sweep point', with no length caveat. Only seed 3's seven points (1.000-1.018: friction 1.0, 3 cm step, pushes) are typical of training. 'Three of the four 128 mm seeds go over inside the training ranges' therefore rests on the two kinds of point that the skeptics qualified.
findings.suggested_fix: After the in-range bullets add: 'The sweep's ramp is a single 20 m climb, longer than any trained ramp (0.8-2.0 m up, then a plateau and a ramp down). x1.1 on every body at once is beyond any whole-robot mass that the per-body draws produced in training (at most about x1.08). On points typical of training, only seed 3 goes over, at 1.000-1.018.' Use the same wording in 'What follows', the review section and the log.

findings.title: 'Run 3's leg had more' headroom is contradicted at the 20-30 ms delays, one of the three factors named in the same sentence
findings.evidence: My script delay.py, run on robustness/results/<run>/sweep_<run>.json.gz at 0.25 m/s, gives heat_worst at 20/30 ms of 128 s0 1.074/1.113, s1 1.127/1.092, s2 1.203/1.224 and s3 1.198/1.220 (mean 1.156, minimum 1.074). Run 3 gives s0 1.236/1.263 and s1 1.199/1.2005 (mean 1.225, minimum 1.199). Run 3's least-loaded delay point is hotter than four of 128 mm's eight. Run 3 s0 also goes over at x1.2 mass (1.030) and with 2 kg (1.010). L188 nevertheless says 'So the real robot's terrain, mass and delay decide how much headroom is left, and run 3's leg had more', and the L40 headline sets 128 mm against 'run 3's 188 mm leg did not'. Both are true only for the nominal and in-range cases and for extra mass, not under delay.
findings.suggested_fix: L188: '... and run 3's leg had more inside the training ranges and under extra mass, but not under delay (20-30 ms: 1.20-1.26 against 1.07-1.22 at 128 mm).' L40: '128 mm runs its drives at about their continuous rating; in the trained conditions run 3's 188 mm leg stayed under it.'

findings.title: The new limitations bullet says each drive's continuous rating is the maker's entry for that drive, but the X6 elbow's comes from the X6-50-L as a stand-in (RD16's confirmed point, still not fixed)
findings.evidence: sim/data/drives.json leg_drives.X6-60.thermal_eq_note reads 'X6-50-L table at 0 rpm used as a stand-in: the V4 X6-60 has no published table'. The front-elbow rating in the env and the sweep is 10.8 = 12.0 x 0.9 (trike_env.py:156; the sweep's settings.continuous_rating_nm 'front elbow' 10.8). The effect on the verdict is small, since the elbow never sets H_all.
findings.suggested_fix: 'each drive's continuous rating comes from the maker's temperature-rise table, the X6 elbow's from the X6-50-L's table as a stand-in (the X6-60 has none published)'.

verdicts.reasoning: The finding holds. The report calls the sweep's ramps 'the trained 3-8 deg ramps' (L46, L175, L396 'trained ramps'), and the log does the same at L223. The text never says that the sweep's ramp is a single climb about 20 m long, while training ramps are 0.8-2.0 m up, followed by a plateau and a ramp down. For a continuous (thermal) rating, how long the load lasts is exactly what matters. On mass, the report says only 'the edge of the training range' (L47) and 'mass x0.9-1.1 per body' (L80). It does not say that x1.1 on every body is about 3.5 SD beyond any whole-robot mass that training produced. The A1, NEW1 and RD1 verdicts each asked for this caveat, and the revision does not include it. Without the ramps and the x1.1 mass point, only fore128-s3 goes over, at 1.0002-1.018. Medium is right: the claim is misleading, but the verdict does not change.
verdicts.evidence: review_d22final3/skeptic/scripts/sweep_check.py, using the limits from run_record env_config (delay 0-10, mass 0.9-1.1, kp 0.9-1.1, force 0.85-1.0, friction 0.3-1.0, |push|<=1.0, step<=0.04, ramp<=10, no payload). It finds 37 in-range points per run, with 0/2/4/11 at 128 mm, 31/28/35/1 at 160 mm and 0/0 for run 3. 128 s1: mass1.1 1.0061, ramp8 1.0201. s2: mass1.1 1.0219, ramp3/5/8 1.0354/1.073/1.1553. s3: mass1.1 1.0642, ramps 1.096/1.1513/1.2165, and 7 other points at 1.0002-1.018. robustness/sweep.py:182-187 builds the ramp box with L=10.0 (half-length) and x0=TERRAIN_EDGE_M=0.6. trike_env.py@f84a6919:196-198 gives terrain_slope_len_m (0.8, 2.0) and a plateau of 0.4-1.5 m, with the up/plateau/down build at :374-383; :724 draws mass_scale with size=m.nbody. scripts/mc_mass.py on trike60_C_closed_capsule_fore128.xml (21 bodies, 12.7506 kg, 200k draws) gives a total-mass scale SD of 0.02861, a maximum of 1.0747 and z(1.1)=3.50. grep of the report, appendix and log finds no '20 m', 'climb', 'sustain' or whole-robot caveat.
